    50	const GITHUB_AUTHORIZATION_URL = 'https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize';
    51	const GITHUB_TOKEN_URL = 'https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token';
    52	const GITHUB_USER_URL = 'https://api.github.com/user';
    53	const GITHUB_EMAILS_URL = 'https://api.github.com/user/emails';
    54	
    55	// ============================================================================
    56	// GitHub-specific Types
    57	// ============================================================================
    58	
    59	interface GitHubTokenResponse {
    60	  access_token: string;
    61	  token_type: string;
    62	  scope: string;
    63	  refresh_token?: string;
    64	  expires_in?: number;
    65	  refresh_token_expires_in?: number;
    66	  error?: string;
    67	  error_description?: string;
    68	}
    69	
    70	interface GitHubUserResponse {
    71	  id: number;
    72	  login: string;
    73	  name: string | null;
    74	  email: string | null;
    75	  avatar_url: string;
    76	}
    77	
    78	interface GitHubEmailResponse {
    79	  email: string;
    80	  primary: boolean;
    81	  verified: boolean;
    82	  visibility: string | null;
    83	}
    84	
    85	// ============================================================================
    86	// GitHub OAuth Provider Implementation
    87	// ============================================================================
    88	
    89	/**
    90	 * GitHub OAuth provider
    91	 */
    92	class GitHubProvider implements OAuthProviderInterface {
    93	  /**
    94	   * Get the GitHub authorization URL with PKCE
    95	   */
    96	  getAuthorizationUrl(
    97	    redirectUri: string,
    98	    state: string,
    99	    codeChallenge: string
   100	  ): string {
   101	    const config = getConfig();
   102	
   103	    const params = new URLSearchParams({
   104	      client_id: config.clientId,
   105	      redirect_uri: redirectUri,
   106	      scope: 'read:user user:email',
   107	      state,
   108	      // GitHub requires PKCE for GitHub Apps but accepts it for OAuth Apps too
   109	      code_challenge: codeChallenge,
   110	      code_challenge_method: 'S256',
   111	    });
   112	
   113	    return `${GITHUB_AUTHORIZATION_URL}?${params.toString()}`;
   114	  }
   115	
   116	  /**
   117	   * Exchange authorization code for tokens
   118	   */
   119	  async exchangeCode(
   120	    code: string,
   121	    redirectUri: string,
   122	    codeVerifier: string
   123	  ): Promise<OAuthTokens> {
   124	    const config = getConfig();
   125	
   126	    const response = await fetch(GITHUB_TOKEN_URL, {
   127	      method: 'POST',
   128	      headers: {
   129	        Accept: 'application/json',
   130	        'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
   131	      },
   132	      body: new URLSearchParams({
   133	        client_id: config.clientId,
   134	        client_secret: config.clientSecret,
   135	        code,
   136	        redirect_uri: redirectUri,
   137	        code_verifier: codeVerifier,
   138	      }),
   139	    });
   140	
   141	    if (!response.ok) {
   142	      throw new OAuthError(
   143	        `GitHub token exchange failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`,
   144	        'token_exchange_failed',
   145	        502
   146	      );
   147	    }
   148	
   149	    const data = (await response.json()) as GitHubTokenResponse;
   150	
   151	    if (data.error) {
   152	      throw new OAuthError(
   153	        data.error_description || data.error,
   154	        data.error,
   155	        400
   156	      );
   157	    }
   158	
   159	    return {
   160	      accessToken: data.access_token,
   161	      refreshToken: data.refresh_token,
   162	      expiresIn: data.expires_in,
   163	      tokenType: data.token_type,
   164	      scope: data.scope,
   165	    };
   166	  }
   167	
   168	  /**
   169	   * Get user info from GitHub
   170	   */
   171	  async getUserInfo(accessToken: string): Promise<OAuthUserInfo> {
   172	    // Fetch user profile
   173	    const userResponse = await fetch(GITHUB_USER_URL, {
   174	      headers: {
   175	        Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
   176	        Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
   177	        'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2022-11-28',
   178	      },
   179	    });
   180	
   181	    if (!userResponse.ok) {
   182	      throw new OAuthError(
   183	        `GitHub user info failed: ${userResponse.status} ${userResponse.statusText}`,
   184	        'user_info_failed',
   185	        502
   186	      );
   187	    }
   188	
   189	    const userData = (await userResponse.json()) as GitHubUserResponse;
   190	
   191	    // Get email - GitHub may not include it in user profile
   192	    let email = userData.email;
   193	
   194	    if (!email) {
   195	      // Fetch emails separately
   196	      const emailsResponse = await fetch(GITHUB_EMAILS_URL, {
   197	        headers: {
   198	          Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
   199	          Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
   200	          'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2022-11-28',
   201	        },
   202	      });
   203	
   204	      if (emailsResponse.ok) {
   205	        const emails = (await emailsResponse.json()) as GitHubEmailResponse[];
   206	        const primaryEmail = emails.find((e) => e.primary && e.verified);
   207	        const verifiedEmail = emails.find((e) => e.verified);
   208	        email = primaryEmail?.email || verifiedEmail?.email || null;
   209	      }
   210	    }
   211	
   212	    if (!email) {
   213	      throw new OAuthError(
   214	        'Could not retrieve email from GitHub. Please ensure your GitHub account has a verified email.',
   215	        'no_email',
   216	        400
   217	      );
   218	    }
   219	
   220	    return {
   221	      id: userData.id.toString(),
   222	      email,
   223	      name: userData.name || userData.login,
   224	      avatarUrl: userData.avatar_url,
   225	    };
   226	  }
   227	}

   230	// Registration
   231	// ============================================================================
   232	
   233	/**
   234	 * GitHub provider instance
   235	 */
   236	export const githubProvider = new GitHubProvider();
   237	
   238	/**
   239	 * Register the GitHub provider
   240	 * Call this during server initialization
   241	 */
   242	export function registerGitHubProvider(): void {
   243	  registerProvider('github', githubProvider);
   244	}
   245	
   246	export default githubProvider;

7:> **Plan version**: **v4** (Planner revision after Architect v3=REVISE + Critic v3=REJECT). Both reviewers converged on 2 surviving CRITICAL blockers from v3: (1) "shared JWT validator" doesn't exist (jose not in shared, JWT_SECRET singleton in server only); (2) AC19 harness has 4 code-grounded bugs (`.pairingUrl` vs CLI's `.connectUrl`, iOS `.onOpenURL` doesn't route `mconnect://pair`, no `session_kill` protocol message, `date +%s%N` not monotonic). v4 pivots auth approach: drops the "shared JWT validator" idea, introduces explicit `local_pairing_auth` v3.1 message so CLI keeps its existing local-pairing-token security model and JWT stays server-only. v4 also rewrites AC19 harness as Node test runner using `process.hrtime.bigint()`, lists CLI/iOS/protocol changes needed for AC19 as Phase 1 deliverables. v4 is the final iteration before max-iteration presentation per skill rule.
37:2. **v3.0 is the protocol baseline; new features land at v3.1 with capability negotiation.** Source of truth: `packages/shared/src/protocol/messages.ts:22` (= `'3.0'`) and `docs/protocol/v3.md`. The CLI catches up to v3.0 in Phase 0 (currently at v2.0, `packages/cli/src/ws/protocol.ts:259`). New `desktop:*` and `worktree:*` message families ship as v3.1 additions and **MUST** include explicit capability negotiation — every client advertises a capability set on auth, server unions them, unknown families to a client are skipped *with a typed `unsupported_capability` warning*, never silent drop. (Today CLI silently `console.warn`s and ignores; that becomes a typed protocol error in v3.1.)
40:5. **Hard gate before UI work.** Phase 0B ends with a packaged-Tauri terminal attach/spawn/resize/kill demo across **mac+linux+win** with iOS attached to the same session. **Kill criterion**: any platform fails attach/resize/kill twice in CI → enter **Phase 0C** (conditional Electron fallback, +1 week) before Phase 1 UI starts. Decision deadline: end of Phase 0B (Day 14). Phase 6 buffer absorbs the +1 week if 0C is triggered.

This produces a credible 12-week scope with the same anchor — explicitly named here so ralph does not silently start cutting other items.
144:- **CLI protocol catch-up + auth state-machine modification**: `packages/cli/src/ws/protocol.ts` updated to `PROTOCOL_VERSION = '3.0'`. **`packages/cli/src/ws/ws-hub.ts:241-275` auth path is modified** (Exception A from §1 principle 1) to accept BOTH v2 query-token URLs (legacy v0.1.10 clients) AND v3 first-message **`local_pairing_auth`** (new desktop/iOS direct-attach clients). **Decision pivot from v3 (Critic-driven)**: do NOT introduce JWT validation into the CLI. CLI keeps its existing local-pairing-token security model in `packages/cli/src/security.ts`. The JWT-based `auth` v3 message (per `packages/shared/src/protocol/messages.ts:62-73`) remains **server-only** (Bun server in `packages/server`); the CLI does not import `jose` or any JWT validator. Instead, **a new v3.1 `local_pairing_auth` message** is added to shared protocol with payload `{ pairingToken: string, version: '3.0', clientCapabilities: string[] }`. CLI validates `pairingToken` against its local registry (existing `packages/cli/src/security.ts` machinery); server's WSHub dispatches `local_pairing_auth` straight to a CLI-compatibility path that bypasses JWT validation. iOS keeps using `auth` (JWT) when connecting to the Bun server; iOS uses `local_pairing_auth` when connecting directly to the CLI via QR. New file `packages/cli/src/ws/auth-bridge.ts` houses CLI-side dual-mode logic (v2 query-token + v3.1 local_pairing_auth); `ws-hub.ts` change is limited to dispatch (≤ 30 lines).

Server-side: new `clientCapabilities: Set<string>` field on `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:59-82` client state; auth-success unions advertised capabilities at `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:660-668`.

   141	### Phase 0A1 — CLI v3 auth migration + capability negotiation (Week 1)
   142	
   143	**Deliverables (scoped, Critic-narrowed — was overloaded in v2 Phase 0A)**:
   144	- **CLI protocol catch-up + auth state-machine modification**: `packages/cli/src/ws/protocol.ts` updated to `PROTOCOL_VERSION = '3.0'`. **`packages/cli/src/ws/ws-hub.ts:241-275` auth path is modified** (Exception A from §1 principle 1) to accept BOTH v2 query-token URLs (legacy v0.1.10 clients) AND v3 first-message **`local_pairing_auth`** (new desktop/iOS direct-attach clients). **Decision pivot from v3 (Critic-driven)**: do NOT introduce JWT validation into the CLI. CLI keeps its existing local-pairing-token security model in `packages/cli/src/security.ts`. The JWT-based `auth` v3 message (per `packages/shared/src/protocol/messages.ts:62-73`) remains **server-only** (Bun server in `packages/server`); the CLI does not import `jose` or any JWT validator. Instead, **a new v3.1 `local_pairing_auth` message** is added to shared protocol with payload `{ pairingToken: string, version: '3.0', clientCapabilities: string[] }`. CLI validates `pairingToken` against its local registry (existing `packages/cli/src/security.ts` machinery); server's WSHub dispatches `local_pairing_auth` straight to a CLI-compatibility path that bypasses JWT validation. iOS keeps using `auth` (JWT) when connecting to the Bun server; iOS uses `local_pairing_auth` when connecting directly to the CLI via QR. New file `packages/cli/src/ws/auth-bridge.ts` houses CLI-side dual-mode logic (v2 query-token + v3.1 local_pairing_auth); `ws-hub.ts` change is limited to dispatch (≤ 30 lines).
   145	- **Capability negotiation** in `packages/shared/src/protocol/messages.ts`: new `client_capabilities` field on auth message; server response unions capabilities; `unsupported_capability` typed error replaces silent `console.warn` drop at `packages/cli/src/ws/ws-hub.ts:524-526`. Server-side: new `clientCapabilities: Set<string>` field on `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:59-82` client state; auth-success unions advertised capabilities at `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:660-668`.

## Summary
v4 fixes several v3 plan defects, but it is not final-passable. The migration, buffer, and Windows-CI issues are mostly addressed at plan level; the remaining blockers are auth scope ambiguity and an AC19 harness that still cannot run as written.

## Analysis
1. **CRITICAL: `local_pairing_auth` is acceptable only for direct CLI attach, but v4 also says Bun server bypasses JWT.**
   - Current shared v3 auth is JWT-first: `packages/shared/src/protocol/messages.ts:65`.
   - Current server validates JWT and derives identity from claims: `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:640`, `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:652`.
   - Server client state requires authenticated identity fields: `packages/server/src/ws/WSHub.ts:64`.
   - v4 line 144 says server WSHub dispatches `local_pairing_auth` through a JWT-bypass path. That introduces an identity/audit bypass unless the server never accepts this message or validates it through an authenticated brokered exchange.
   - v4 line 711 says “CLI handles ONLY this,” which conflicts with line 144. The secure answer is: CLI accepts `local_pairing_auth`; Bun server remains JWT-only.

2. **CRITICAL: AC19 still is not mechanically executable.**
   - The plan uses `xcodebuild -scheme MConnect-Test`: `.omc/...md:551`, but the repo only has the `MConnect` shared scheme: `packages/ios-app/MConnect.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/MConnect.xcscheme:20`.
   - The plan launches `com.lecoder.MConnect`: `.omc/...md:575`, `.omc/...md:577`, but the actual bundle id is lowercase `com.lecoder.mconnect`: `packages/ios-app/MConnect.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:586`.
   - The plan passes `MCONNECT_TEST_AUTOKILL=1` as an app argument: `.omc/...md:577`; for simulator runtime env, this needs `SIMCTL_CHILD_MCONNECT_TEST_AUTOKILL=1` in the `spawnSync` environment.
   - The shown spec also calls undefined helpers (`readUntilJson`, `waitForProbe`, `sleep`) at `.omc/...md:558`, `.omc/...md:564`, `.omc/...md:571`.

3. **MAJOR #1 migration runner: fixed honestly.**
   - Current `SessionStore` owns the DB handle and runs inline migration bootstrapping: `packages/cli/src/session/SessionStore.ts:49`, `packages/cli/src/session/SessionStore.ts:56`.
   - Current `001_sessions.sql` uses bare `CREATE TABLE`: `packages/cli/migrations/001_sessions.sql:8`.
   - v4’s library `runMigrations(db, migrationsDir)` called by `SessionStore` is the right shape: `.omc/...md:171`.

4. **MAJOR #2 buffer accounting: fixed.**
   - v4 has explicit 14/15/16-week calendars: `.omc/...md:398` through `.omc/...md:403`.

5. **MAJOR #3 Windows CI: directionally sufficient, but YAML wording needs tightening.**
   - Current CI has Ubuntu and macOS jobs, no Windows desktop hard gate: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:24`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:217`.
   - v4 adds `.github/workflows/desktop-hard-gate.yml`: `.omc/...md:229`.
   - Do not implement literal `runs-on: [macos-14, ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest]`; use `strategy.matrix.os` and `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`.

## Root Cause
v4 fixed the previous “missing deliverable” pattern, but still treats plan text as executable proof in two places where platform/runtime details matter: server auth identity semantics and iOS Simulator execution mechanics.

## Recommendations
1. **Revise auth wording and gates** - small effort - high impact  
   Remove server-side `local_pairing_auth` JWT bypass. Add explicit tests: Bun server rejects `local_pairing_auth`; CLI WSHub accepts it only when token matches the active local session token.

2. **Rewrite AC19 command details** - small effort - high impact  
   Use scheme `MConnect`, bundle id `com.lecoder.mconnect`, `SIMCTL_CHILD_MCONNECT_TEST_AUTOKILL=1`, and include/import helper functions in the spec.

3. **Make Windows CI YAML exact** - small effort - medium impact  
   Replace prose `runs-on` array with a concrete matrix skeleton.

## Trade-offs
| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| CLI-only `local_pairing_auth` | Preserves existing local-token security, avoids server identity bypass | Direct CLI/server auth paths stay different |
| Server accepts `local_pairing_auth` | One message type everywhere | Requires new identity-binding design; current v4 would bypass JWT/audit semantics |
| Keep AC19 as current pseudocode | Faster planning close | Fails immediately in CI |
| Make AC19 exact now | Reliable Phase 1 gate | Slightly more planning detail |

## Consensus Addendum
- **Antithesis (steelman):** v4 is much closer than v3; the auth pivot is architecturally better than forcing JWT into CLI, and AC19 now names real deliverables instead of hand-waving.
- **Tradeoff tension:** Keeping CLI local-pairing auth simple conflicts with having a uniform server protocol. The synthesis is dual auth by endpoint, not JWT bypass inside the server.
- **Synthesis:** CLI direct attach uses `local_pairing_auth`; Bun server remains JWT-first; shared protocol documents both as endpoint-scoped flows.
- **Principle violations (deliberate mode):** Critical: server JWT-bypass ambiguity violates security-by-default. Critical: AC19 violates mechanical executability.
